intro.title: Utility Types
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays user profile information, such as name, age, and email. You will learn how to use TypeScript utility types like `Partial`, `Readonly`, and `Pick` to make your code more flexible and type-safe. The main technologies involved are Vue 3 with TypeScript, focusing on defining and manipulating interfaces. By the end, you'll understand how utility types help manage and transform object shapes in your components.
intro.usecase: Utility types in Vue are essential for building robust form systems in applications like e-commerce checkouts or user registration flows. When handling form data, developers use utility types to create strict interfaces for user inputs, validation states, and submission payloads. For example, in a dashboard settings panel, utility types ensure that user preferences are correctly typed when saving to backend APIs or updating UI components reactively. This prevents runtime errors and provides better TypeScript autocompletion during development.
